newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Swedish GDP seen up 0.9 pct Q4 '96.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Swedish GDP seen up 0.9 pct Q4 '96.

text.p: Seasonally adjusted Swedish gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to have risen 0.9 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 from the third quarter, according to a Reuter poll of economists.
Fourth quarter GDP is expected to have risen 1.7 percent from the corresponding quarter in 1995.
Economists gave a range for the quarterly increase of 0.4 percent to 1.2 percent, and for the year-on-year rise of between 1.0 percent and 2.5 percent.
In the third quarter of 1996, seasonally adjusted GDP rose 0.7 percent from the second quarter for a year-on-year rate of 0.8 percent.
In the fourth quarter of 1995, seasonally adjusted GDP was flat and the annual rate was 2.9 percent. For the full year 1995, GDP rose on average 3.6 percent.
For 1996, economists see seasonally adjusted GDP rising 1.4 percent on average, with a range of between 1.1 to 1.7 percent.
Next year they expect a 2.4 percent increase on average, with forecasts ranging from 2.0 percent to 3.3 percent.
Statistics Sweden will release fourth quarter GDP figures at 1200 GMT on March 12.

Economists interviewed came from Carnegie, Consensus, Den Danske Bank, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Nomura Bank, Nordbanken, PaineWebber, S-E-Banken, Swedbank, Transferator, Unibors Markets, and Ohman Fondkommission.
Den Danske Bank, Hagstromer & Qviberg, S-E-Banken, Swedbank and Unibank Markets did not give quarterly figures while Consensus and S-E-Banken did not give an average forecasts for 1997.
